chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from Muhammad ibn Isa, from Yunus, from one of his companions, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
I asked him: Is it permissible for the fox, the rabbit, or any of the wild beasts to touch (one), whether alive or dead? He said: It does not harm him, but he should wash his hand.
ai.seo_question: Does touching a fox or rabbit make you impure in Shia fiqh?
ai.summary: In this narration from al-Kafi, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) clarifies the fiqh of contact with wild beasts (al-siba'), ruling that their touch does not impart ritual impurity (najasah) but requires washing the hand as a precautionary measure (istihbab). This ruling distinguishes these animals from the dog, whose saliva is considered strictly impure, reflecting the Shia scholarly emphasis on distinguishing between inherent impurity and recommended purification practices. The hadith underscores the principle that not all animal contact necessitates full ablution or washing, aligning with the broader juristic discourse on the purity of the body and clothes.
